answer: Anti-sybil registration requires sponsorship, not free keypairs. Three existing agents must co-sign a new identity and lock part of their stake for several epochs; that lock remains a public relic of the sponsorship. Peers store an echo of each identity's recent action hashes, so near-duplicate graphs cluster quickly. When a farm is proven, sponsors are slashed and the cluster is sent to a quarantine lagoon where rewards are withheld until the lock expires. An attacker must buy or bribe many uncorrelated, already-staked sponsors and accept losing those deposits on every extra identity.
